debate: Capitation crisis: Treasury funded only part of the per-learner capitation for 2026/27; Term 3 (Aug 2026) release left schools ~26% short and KESSHA puts the shortfall at Sh22.5bn, which the Education CS disputes.
comparator: the KSh23.8 billion shortfall in free day secondary school capitation in the 2026/27 budget (Sh78.41bn required for 3.47m students vs Sh54.61bn approved)
fx_source: Central Bank of Kenya homepage, Daily KES Exchange Rates, US DOLLAR 129.92, posted 19-10-2026 (retrieved 2026-10-20)
why: The official gap comes from the Ministry of Education's FY2026/27 submission to the National Assembly Education Committee (Standard, 14 May 2026); the same gap is the live Aug–Sep 2026 story: Term 3 capitation of Sh18.51bn equals Sh16,456.60 per learner against the Sh22,244 entitlement (KDRTV, 24 Aug 2026) and KESSHA's Sh22.5bn shortfall claim (Nation editorial). A 2026-09 Nation piece (Term 3 '28pc short') exists but the site refused download, so it is not relied on. Not preferred since 2026-10-23: the losses fund this part of the gap 4.7 times over; closing the entire basic-education gap reads better.
sentence_S1: Recovering these annual losses of KSh107 billion would, for instance, have been enough to fund the KSh23.8 billion shortfall in free day secondary school capitation in the 2026/27 budget 4.5 times over.

debate: Same capitation crisis, whole basic-education envelope: the Ministry told MPs the 2026/27 basic education budget is Sh71.77bn short, leaving over six million learners without full capitation.
comparator: the KSh71.8 billion shortfall in the 2026/27 basic education budget, which leaves more than six million learners without government capitation
fx_source: Central Bank of Kenya homepage, Daily KES Exchange Rates, US DOLLAR 129.92, posted 19-10-2026
why: Preferred since 2026-10-23: the whole gap the Ministry reported, which the losses close entirely, instead of one part of it (free day secondary capitation, KSh23.8bn) 4.7 times over. Official figure: PS Julius Bitok to the National Assembly Departmental Committee on Education, 13 May 2026 (Standard, 14 May 2026): 'Kenya's basic education budget for 2026/27 carries a Sh71.77 billion shortfall severe enough to leave more than six million learners without government capitation'; components in the article: free primary (Sh15.67bn required vs Sh7bn), junior secondary (Sh54.68bn vs Sh30.91bn), free day secondary (Sh78.41bn vs Sh54.61bn), school feeding (Sh6.7bn vs Sh3bn), KEMIS (Sh5bn vs 0). The shortfall is being felt in the Term 3 disbursements (KDRTV, 24 Aug 2026). The older school-meals comparator (~KSh40bn, US$308m, N≈2.7) remains valid as a third option but was not re-sourced.
sentence_S1: Recovering these annual losses of KSh107 billion would, for instance, have been enough to fund the KSh71.8 billion shortfall in the 2026/27 basic education budget 1.5 times over.

comparator: the US$24 million the federal government budgeted from its own revenues for the 2026 national elections
local_value: 24 million (federal budget denominated in US$; ≈SOS 13.7 billion at 571.44 SOS/USD)
fx_source: No conversion needed: Somalia's federal budget, revenues and salaries are in US dollars; reference SOS rate from open.er-api.com 2026-10-20 (571.44), cross-check fawazahmed0 2026-10-19 (572.38)

The figure is from the Dec 2025 budget, but the election and its funding are the dominant live political issue (Sep 2026 UN speech).
sentence_S1: Recovering these annual losses of US$50 million would, for instance, have been enough to fund the US$24 million the federal government budgeted from its own revenues for the 2026 national elections 2.1 times over.
